questions.question: Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP), founded in 1903, to carry on the work of social reform was active in which of the following states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Shree Narayana Dharma Paripalana Yogam (SNDP)** was founded in 1903 by **Sree Narayana Guru**, a social reformer and spiritual leader from Kerala.
 
• The organization was established to work for the **upliftment of the Ezhava community**, a marginalized group in Kerala, and to promote social equality and education.
 
• SNDP played a significant role in the **social reform movements of Kerala**, advocating for the eradication of caste discrimination and promoting the idea of "One Caste, One Religion, One God."
 
• The SNDP Yogam contributed to the **educational and economic empowerment** of the Ezhava community by establishing schools, colleges, and other institutions.
 
• The organization's influence was instrumental in shaping the **progressive social landscape of modern Kerala**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sree Narayana Guru**:

 
 
• Sree Narayana Guru was a **philosopher, spiritual leader, and social reformer** from Kerala, revered for his efforts to fight caste discrimination.
 
• He is best known for his message of universal brotherhood and his teaching of "**One Caste, One Religion, One God for Humanity**."
 
• He consecrated temples that were open to all, breaking traditional caste barriers in worship.
 
 
 
• **Social Reform Movements in Kerala**:
 
 
• Kerala witnessed various social reform movements in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, focusing on **abolishing caste discrimination** and promoting education.
 
• Prominent movements include the **SNDP movement**, the efforts of Chattampi Swamikal, and the Vaikom Satyagraha.
 
 
 
• **Ezhava Community**:
 
 
• The Ezhavas are a prominent community in Kerala who were historically marginalized due to caste-based discrimination.
 
• They benefitted greatly from the social reforms spearheaded by Sree Narayana Guru and the SNDP Yogam.
 
 
 
• **SNDP's Contributions**:
 
 
• The SNDP Yogam established various institutions like **schools, colleges, and cooperative societies** to improve the socio-economic status of the Ezhava community.
 
• It also played a role in Kerala's political and cultural awakening during the early 20th century.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Paramhansa Mandalis is INCORRECT?

options.text: They were primarily interested in breaking caste rules.
Its founders did not believe in God.
It was founded in 1849 in Maharashtra.
They also advocated for widow remarriage and women’s education.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Its founders did not believe in God**__.

__
 
• Paramahansa Mandali was a secret socio-religious group, established in 1849, in Bombay .
 
• It is closely related to Manav Dharma Sabha which was found in 1844 in Surat.
 
• It was started by Durgaram Mehtaji, Dadoba Pandurang and a group of his friends.
 
• The members of the organization believed in One god.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• They supported widow remarriage.
 
• The member of the organization used to take food prepared by lower-caste people

questions.question: The ______ was started by the Sikh reformers to purify their religious places by removing the evil social practices that had slowly crept into them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Akali Movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Akali Movement was started in the early 20th century by Sikh reformers.**
 
• The primary aim was to liberate **Sikh gurdwaras from the control of corrupt priests who were influenced by British rule in India.**
 
• The movement sought to **remove social evils and restore the purity of religious practices that had slipped into the gurdwaras.**
 
• The movement led to the **Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925, which transferred the control of gurdwaras to the elected bodies of the Sikh community.**
 
• This movement played a crucial role in awakening the **masses and strengthening the spirit of freedom, which eventually contributed to the broader Indian independence movement.**
 
• The **Akali Movement not only focused on religious reform but also brought political and social change, leading to a greater sense of unity among Sikhs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Movement
 Key Points
 
 
 
 

 Namdhari Movement
 
 
Started in the mid-19th century by Baba Ram Singh.

 
It was a socio-religious reform movement among the Sikhs and an early rebellion against British rule.

 
Namdharis are also known as "Kuka" because of their unique style of reciting the "Kirtan."

 
 
 

 Ghadar Movement
 
 
Formed in 1913 by Indian immigrants from the United States and Canada.

 
Its objective was to overthrow British colonial authority in India by means of an armed revolution.

 
Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and Bhagat Singh were among its key leaders.

 
 
 

 Nirankari Movement
 
 
Began in the early 19th century as a reform movement within Sikhism.

 
It emphasized the worship of God as Nirankar (formless), rejecting the belief in avatars.

 
The movement eventually separated from mainstream Sikhism and became an independent spiritual path.

questions.question: Which of the following social organisations was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Arya Samaj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati on **10 April 1875** in Bombay (now Mumbai).
 
• The primary aim of Arya Samaj was to reform Hinduism by eliminating orthodox rituals and promoting the teachings of the Vedas.
 
• Swami Dayananda Saraswati's motto for Arya Samaj was "Krinvanto Vishwam Aryam," which means "Make the World Noble."
 
• Arya Samaj was instrumental in promoting social reforms such as women's education, widow remarriage, and the abolition of the caste system.
 
• The organization also played a significant role in the Indian independence movement by fostering a sense of nationalism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swami Dayananda Saraswati**

 
 
• Born on 12 February 1824 in Tankara, Gujarat.
 
• He was a prominent Hindu religious leader and the founder of the Arya Samaj.
 
• His ideologies were based on the teachings of the Vedas and he advocated for the return to the Vedic way of life.
 
• He wrote the book "Satyarth Prakash," which translates to "The Light of Truth," outlining his religious philosophy.
 
 
 
• **Vedas**
 
 
• The Vedas are a large body of religious texts originating in ancient India.
 
• There are four Vedas: Rigveda, Samaveda, Yajurveda, and Atharvaveda.
 
• They are composed in Vedic Sanskrit and form the oldest layer of Sanskrit literature.
 
• The Vedas are considered the oldest scriptures of Hinduism and contain hymns, philosophy, and guidance on rituals.
 
 
 
• **Social Reforms by Arya Samaj**
 
 
• Abolition of child marriage and promotion of widow remarriage.
 
• Advocated for women’s education and gender equality.
 
• Emphasized on the removal of untouchability and caste discrimination.
 
• Promoted the use of Hindi and other regional languages in education.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj’s Role in Indian Independence**
 
 
• Arya Samaj members actively participated in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• Many of its leaders were involved in the Swadeshi movement and the boycott of British goods.
 
• The organization fostered a sense of nationalism and pride in Indian culture and heritage.
 
• It also opposed British colonial policies and worked towards social and educational reforms.

questions.question: Who among the following was the pioneer of 'Bhoodan Movement'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acharya Vinoba Bhave**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Acharya Vinoba Bhave** was the pioneer of the **Bhoodan Movement**, which aimed at redistributing land to landless farmers.
 
• The movement began in **1951** at Pochampally village in Telangana, where Vinoba Bhave persuaded wealthy landowners to donate land for the poor.
 
• The term "Bhoodan" translates to "**Land Donation**" and was a non-violent initiative inspired by Gandhian philosophy.
 
• Vinoba Bhave walked across villages, requesting landowners to donate a part of their land voluntarily to the landless, promoting **social equality**.
 
• By 1954, the movement expanded into the **Gramdan Movement**, where entire villages donated land for community welfare.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vinoba Bhave** was a spiritual leader and a prominent disciple of Mahatma Gandhi, deeply committed to the principles of non-violence and selfless service.
 
• The **Bhoodan Movement** was a part of larger Gandhian efforts to address rural poverty and land inequality in post-independence India.
 
• The movement significantly influenced the concept of **land reforms** in India, although its success varied across regions.
 
• The **Gramdan Movement**, derived from Bhoodan, aimed to promote collective ownership of land and community-driven development.
 
• Vinoba Bhave received the **Ramon Magsaysay Award** for his social and leadership efforts in 1958.

questions.question: Brahmo Samaj, the theistic movement within Hinduism, was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in the year ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1828**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Brahmo Samaj** was founded by **Raja Ram Mohan Roy** in the year **1828**.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj was a **reformist and theistic movement** within Hinduism, aiming to bring about **social, political, and religious changes**.
 
• It promoted the belief in a **formless, eternal, and omnipresent God** and rejected idol worship and meaningless rituals.
 
• **Raja Ram Mohan Roy**, often regarded as the **Father of the Indian Renaissance**, was instrumental in initiating this reform movement to modernize Hindu society.
 
• The Brahmo Samaj played a significant role in the abolition of **social evils like Sati**, child marriage, and caste discrimination.
 
• It emphasized the importance of **education**, particularly for women, and encouraged **scientific inquiry** and rational thinking.
 
• The movement also advocated for **monotheism**, equality, and the elimination of superstitions in Indian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **1839**__

 __
 
• This year does not relate to the foundation of the Brahmo Samaj. However, it was a period marked by significant reformist activities in India.
 
 
 
• **1856**__
 __
 
• In this year, the **Widow Remarriage Act** was passed under the guidance of **Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar**, another prominent social reformer.
 
 
 
• **1879**__
 
 
• No significant event related to the Brahmo Samaj occurred in this year. However, by this time, the Brahmo Samaj had split into two factions: **Adi Brahmo Samaj** and **Sadharan Brahmo Samaj**.

questions.question: The Satnami Movement in Central India had a motive to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** **____**improve social status of leatherworkers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Ghasidas started the Satnami movement in central India to improve the social status of leather workers.
 
• ​The most-important Satnami group was founded in 1820 in the Chattisgarh region of middle India by Ghasidas, a farm servant and member of the Chamar caste.
 
• His Satnam Panth (“Path of the True Name”) succeeded in providing a religious and social identity for large numbers of Chattisgarhi Chamars.
 
• Ghasidas is remembered for having thrown images of Hindu gods onto a rubbish heap. 
 
• He preached a code of ethical and dietary self-restraint and social equality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Guru Balakdas was the son of the founder of the Chhattisgarh Satnampanth, Guru Ghasidas.
 
• Haridasa Thakur was a prominent Vaishnava saint known for being instrumental in the initial propagation of the Hare Krishna movement.

questions.question: Which social reformer from South India founded the Self Respect Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**EV Ramaswamy Naicker**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **EV Ramaswamy Naicker**, also known as Periyar, was a prominent social reformer from South India.
 
• He founded the **Self Respect Movement** in 1925 to promote social equality and fight against caste discrimination.
 
• The movement aimed to instill a sense of pride and dignity among the oppressed classes, challenging the existing social norms and practices.
 
• Periyar was a staunch advocate for women's rights and worked tirelessly for the eradication of untouchability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Self Respect Movement**

 
 
• Launched in Tamil Nadu, this movement sought to achieve a society where backward castes have equal human rights, and encouraging them to have self-respect.
 
• It played a crucial role in promoting rationalism and anti-Brahminism.
 
• The movement opposed the concept of the superiority of Brahmins and other upper castes.
 
• It also worked towards the upliftment of women and advocated for their education and equal rights.
 
 
 
• **Periyar's Legacy**
 
 
• Periyar's ideas and principles continue to influence many social and political movements in Tamil Nadu and other parts of India.
 
• He is regarded as the father of the Dravidian movement.
 
• His works have been translated into several languages and continue to inspire activists fighting for social justice.
 
 
 
• **Rationalism**
 
 
• Rationalism is the practice or principle of basing opinions and actions on reason and knowledge rather than on religious belief or emotional response.
 
• Periyar advocated for rationalism, rejecting religious dogmas and superstitions.
 
• He believed that rational thinking was essential for social progress and equality.
 
 
 
• **Anti-Caste Movements in India**
 
 
• Anti-caste movements have a long history in India, aimed at eradicating the caste system and promoting social equality.
 
• Other notable leaders of anti-caste movements include Dr. B.R. Ambedkar and Jyotirao Phule.
 
• These movements have significantly contributed to the socio-political fabric of India, advocating for the rights of the oppressed and marginalized communities.

questions.question: Who said, ‘One caste, one religion, one God for humankind’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shree Narayana Guru**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narayana Guru**, IPA, was a **philosopher**, **spiritual leader**, and **social reformer in India**.
 
• He led a reform movement against injustice in the caste-ridden society of **Kerala **in order to **promote spiritual enlightenment **and **social equality**.
 
• He was **born on 20 August 1856**, **Chempazhanthy **in **Thiruvananthapuram**, and **died on 20 September 1928**, in **Sivagiri, Kerala**.
 
• He coined the slogan “**One Caste, One Religion, One God for All” **to combat caste injustice (**Oru Jathi, Oru Matham, Oru Daivam, Manushyanu**).
 
• **In 1888**, he constructed a **temple in Aruvippuram devoted **to **Lord Shiva**, **defying the caste-based norms of the time**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohandas Karamchand Gandhi **was an **Indian lawyer**, **anti-colonial nationalist**, and **political ethicist **who **employed nonviolent resistance **to lead the **successful campaign **for **India's independence **from **British rule **and to l**ater inspire movements **for **civil rights and freedom across the world**.
 
• **Jyotirao Govindrao Phule**, also known as **Mahatma Jyotiba Phule **was an **Indian social activist**, **thinker**, **anti-caste social reformer**, and **writer from Maharashtra**.
 
• **Rajendra Prasad **was an **Indian politician**, **lawyer**, **Indian independence activist**, **journalist **& **scholar who served as the first president **of the **Republic of India from 1950 to 1962**.
